clue.text: Miss Trotwood's friend reportedly has rubbish on order

indicators.note: reportedly tells us to take the friend's name as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: in Dickens's David Copperfield, Betsey Trotwood's lodger and friend is Mr Dick
tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A Dickens character's companion is apparently waiting on a delivery of junk he has ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Dick is Betsey Trotwood's lodger in Dickens's David Copperfield; 'reportedly' says his name is only heard. Tat is British slang for tawdry rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed by authority, a peremptory command.

clue.text: Two, we hear, at Royal Academy on the up in erstwhile capital

indicators.note: we hear says the name supplied by the cross-reference is taken by its sound

parts.note: the clue numbered 2 (2-down) is defined as Jack, the novelist's first name

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
RA is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A pair of people at the Royal Academy are on the rise in some former seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' points to 2-down, whose definition is Jack; said aloud it gives DJAK. 'on the up' turns AT + RA into ARTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Djakarta, now spelt Jakarta, was Indonesia's capital city until the government moved to Nusantara.

clue.text: Jack — roué, perhaps? Judge not

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the two words might be arranged otherwise, with something set aside

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letter pool
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: Was this Jack a debauchee? Don't be quick to condemn him, the clue warns.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle JACK ROUE and take out J (judge, 'not' marking its removal): the remaining seven letters spell the Beat novelist's surname. The whole clue also describes him, echoing 'Judge not, that ye be not judged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Kerouac, author of On the Road, lived a notoriously dissolute life, so roué fits him.

clue.text: What you might hear in Davos about Rhône plan

definitions.text: What you might hear in Davos

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of these two words are reordered

explanation.surface: A Swiss resort hears gossip about a scheme for the river Rhône.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhône rises in Switzerland, which makes the surface plausible; 'about' rearranges RHONEPLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The long wooden horn is a traditional Swiss mountain instrument, heard in resorts like Davos.

clue.text: It's unusual to book an opera in Alabama

indicators.note: in says the book and opera are placed within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: Booking a night at the opera in Alabama would be an odd thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what departs from the norm, odd or atypical.

clue.text: Worst types into agitating; were they?

definitions.text: Worst types into agitating; were they?

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them, to beat them
genera are types or classes

indicators.note: agitating stirs the letters of the following word into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether the lowest kinds of people were drawn into agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitating' shakes INTO into TION. Read whole, the clue asks whether these were bad types given to agitating, as their critics said.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beat writers of the 1950s were seen by critics as degenerate agitators against conformity.

clue.text: Wooden character, one created by Hardy, with English name

parts.note: Gabriel Oak is the shepherd hero of Thomas Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd

explanation.surface: A stiff figure from a Hardy novel is given an English name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' tempts as a description of the character, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of oak timber is wooden.

clue.text: Mystic manipulator seen turning up French street after religious service

indicators.note: after places the street behind the service in the answer

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A spiritual healer is spotted wandering up a Paris street once church is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the French street because this is a down clue. 'Mystic' colours the definition: a masseur's healing hands can seem almost magical.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage therapist manipulates muscles with the hands, sometimes with a near-mystical aura of healing.

clue.text: Where Rembrandt started to line a study?

parts.note: a ley, as in ley line, is a line linking ancient sites
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Asks where the painter began by drawing a line in his workroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' looks like the start of a letter selection, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was born in Leiden in the Netherlands, an older spelling of the town's name.

clue.text: With Latin version of lissom rogue is one seen in Roman comedy

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A supple rascal appears in a Latin edition of some classical farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges L plus LISSOMROGUEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plautus's comedy Miles Gloriosus features the boastful soldier, a stock figure of Roman theatre.

clue.text: Empress, one to hold onto quietly in Austria

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, one
to grip is to hold on to tightly
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: An empress clings softly to something while in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: Austria had empresses, making 'in Austria' look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrippina the Younger was a Roman empress, wife of Claudius and mother of Nero.

clue.text: Novelist needing directions in Kentucky, although born in Colorado

indicators.note: in places the compass directions within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky
ESE, east-south-east, combines compass directions

explanation.surface: A writer needs guidance around Kentucky, despite being a Colorado native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although born in Colorado' adds only a fact: Ken Kesey was born in La Junta, Colorado, not Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Kesey wrote One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.

clue.text: Somervillians Murdoch, Sayers, etc, needing energy after manual labouring

indicators.note: after puts the energy letter behind the reworked letters
labouring suggests the word is worked hard until its letters change order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Famous Oxford women writers need a burst of vigour after hard physical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labouring' rearranges MANUAL into ALUMNA. Somerville is an Oxford college; Iris Murdoch and Dorothy L Sayers studied there.
explanation.definitionFit: Former female students of a college are its graduates, and these women studied at Somerville.

clue.text: General directions taken about Ohio, finding one like Columbus

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for general

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the directions wrap around the state

parts.note: ENE and SE are two compass directions

explanation.surface: A commander travels round Ohio, discovering someone like the famous explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbus, Ohio, makes the state look relevant to the definition; but Columbus the navigator was born in Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Columbus was a native of Genoa, so he was a Genoese.

clue.text: Astronomer making nasty choices to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stargazer is making some unpleasant decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'making' into the definition; it is a link word joining definition and wordplay, since 'Astronomer making' does not stand for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tycho Brahe was the Danish astronomer known by his first name.

clue.text: One of the five here makes one snigger uproariously about start of book

indicators.note: about here means around, so the scrambled letters surround the book's first letter
uproariously suggests riotous disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order
start of says only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: One poet's reading makes a listener laugh wildly at the opening of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uproariously' rearranges SNIGGER as GINSERG, which goes 'about' B. The five are the Beat writers in this grid: Ginsberg, Burroughs, Snyder, Kerouac and Kesey.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg, author of Howl, was a leading figure of the Beat movement.

clue.text: Digs, we've heard, one of the five here

indicators.note: we've heard says the word for digs is taken as it sounds, not spelt

parts.note: a creature that digs tunnels burrows

explanation.surface: Lodgings, someone says, belong to one of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like the British noun for lodgings, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: William S Burroughs, author of Naked Lunch, was one of the Beat writers.

clue.text: "The loveliest spot that man hath ever found" with marijuana mostly found by a lake

definitions.text: "The loveliest spot that man hath ever found"

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: grass is slang for marijuana
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A poet's praise for a beauty spot is paired with dope smoked beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Wordsworth on Grasmere, a village and lake in the English Lake District, where he lived at Dove Cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth used these words of the Lake District village where he made his home.

clue.text: "While the cock (…)to the stack, or the -, / Stoutly struts his dames before" (Milton, L'Allegro)

definitions.text: "While the cock (…)to the stack, or the -, / Stoutly struts his dames before" (Milton, L'Allegro)

parts.words: "While the cock (…)to the stack, or the -, / Stoutly struts his dames before" (Milton, L'Allegro)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing words name the farm entrance the cockerel struts towards in Milton's poem

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the dash marks the two words missing from Milton's lines in L'Allegro.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's cock struts to the big doorway of a farm building where grain was stored.

clue.text: Help one up to part of the circle to see Stoppard play

parts.note: an arc is part of a circle's circumference

indicators.note: in a down clue up means these words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: aid is help
A is the indefinite article, one

explanation.surface: Someone helps a companion up to the circle seats at the theatre to watch a Stoppard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AID + A to give ADIA; 'the circle' sounds like a theatre balcony but is geometric.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a 1993 play by Tom Stoppard.

clue.text: One term for Frost, right?

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain word is a proper name for frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost is also Robert Frost, the American poet, and a rimer is a writer of rhymes: the whole clue defines him.
explanation.definitionFit: A rimer, an old spelling of rhymer, is a poet, which Robert Frost was.

clue.text: Old Portuguese ready to have Gustave following me in Paris

indicators.note: following places the artist's name after the French word

parts.note: moi is French for me
Gustave Doré was the French illustrator

explanation.surface: A Portuguese man is happy to have the French artist come after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' here is slang for money (as in 'readies'), so 'Old Portuguese ready' is an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The moidore was a gold coin of Portugal, current in the 18th century.

clue.text: Doctor Syn embarrassedto rear one of the five here

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the name are altered
in a down clue to rear is to rise up, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: red means embarrassed, as in red-faced; the clue prints this run-together with the link 'to'

explanation.surface: The fictional smuggler-vicar Doctor Syn blushes as he rears up, one of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges SYN as SNY; 'rear' turns RED into DER. Doctor Syn is a fictional vicar-smuggler; the clue prints 'embarrassedto' as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary Snyder, the poet, is one of the Beat writers.

clue.text: In returning to company misrepresent, we hear, his version of Merry Wives

indicators.note: returning says the little word is turned back to front
we hear says the word for misrepresent is taken by its sound

parts.note: to lie is to misrepresent

explanation.surface: Lying about returning to a firm, a composer works on a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IN into NI; LIE is heard as LAI. The definition is the composer whose version, the opera, was The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Nicolai composed the opera The Merry Wives of Windsor (1849).

clue.text: Political theorist the Spanish josh unendingly

parts.note: las is a Spanish word for the (feminine plural)

indicators.note: unendingly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to josh is to kid, to tease

explanation.surface: A political thinker teases the Spanish without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unendingly' looks like 'without end' in the sense of forever, but it trims KID to KI.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Laski was a British political scientist at the LSE and Labour Party chairman.

clue.text: Really hot books by Miller

definitions.meaning: the hottest parts of the world, the equatorial zone
Henry Miller wrote Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn

explanation.surface: Some of Miller's novels are seriously steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Miller's two Tropic novels were banned as obscene, so 'Really hot' works on both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The equatorial belt between Cancer and Capricorn is hot; Miller's novels share the name.

clue.text: Birds to cook at parties

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
dos are parties or celebrations

explanation.surface: Some birds are to be cooked at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The extinct dodo is hardly a party dish: the surface is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius.

clue.text: Flyer for a Gallico novella

definitions.meaning: a white Arctic wildfowl species that flies
Paul Gallico wrote the 1941 novella about a bird and Dunkirk

explanation.surface: A bird gives its name to a short novel by Paul Gallico.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a white Arctic goose, and Gallico's novella is titled after one.

clue.text: Most promptly, one's into author of Gold! a second time

indicators.note: into says the one-letter piece goes inside the author's name

parts.note: Charles Reade wrote the play Gold! (1853)
I is the Roman numeral for one
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: One enthusiast immerses themselves again in a Victorian writer's play, as fast as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's into' means I is into READE, giving READIE; 'a second time' is S + T, not 'again'.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiest means quickest or most willing; readily and promptly are near synonyms.

clue.text: Directions for one in ancient Jewish sect

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
S is south, a compass direction
SE is south-east, a compass direction
NE is north-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions for joining an old religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' reads as instructions but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish group of the Second Temple period.
